analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md in the runtime-constants table (head lines ~1968-1971). It moves the reconnect backoff source reference to CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift and adds two rows: backoff reset after a 60 s stable session (counted from the register frame) and a random 0..1 s reconnect wait after close code 1012 without growing the backoff. The ping/pong row now points at CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift. No code, auth, attestation, encryption or key-handling behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

The supplied units are the base text of surrounding sections (logout/revoke, stop/restart drain, addon hold, autopilot, doctor and the rest). They are unchanged context, so I did not treat them as new behavior. Their documented security properties are consistent with the threat model: logout sends the token only to the recorded issuer, follows no redirects, and confirms revocation only on HTTP 204; drain stops the process before revocation; the add-on hold socket is local.

The documented reconnect change touches TB-002 availability and TB-011/T-053 connection-bound authorization. The 1012 jitter and the backoff reset could affect the reconnect-storm load on the coordinator. A reconnect must still require fresh proof and a fresh authorization grant, and the docs make no claim to the contrary. I cannot verify that CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift actually implements the documented values or that the code paths reset authorization state, since the source is not supplied. This is a documentation-only change, so I report no regression, but the next pass should verify the code against the doc if the code is in the same PR.
